newsitem.title: USA: Mothers charge Scouts in NY sexual abuse.
newsitem.headline: Mothers charge Scouts in NY sexual abuse.

text.p: Three mothers said Tuesday they were suing the Boy Scouts of America for $72 million alleging that their sons were sexually assaulted at summer camp by other boys after being lured into a cabin on a promise they could win a dollar.

The mothers and their attorney told a news conference that six boys between the ages of 6 and 10 were sodomized with a broom handle by older Boy Scouts while 20 other boys watched but did not help them.
A spokesman for Boy Scouts of America declined to comment on the legal issues surrounding the alleged incidents but did answer some of the charges related to its policies.
The alleged incidents occurred in August last year at Camp Keowa for underprivileged inner-city children in Narrowsburg, New York.

"These were shocking premeditated sexual attacks," said attorney Michael Feldman, who filed the lawsuit in Bronx Count Court Monday. "They were lured into the cabin with the promise they could win a dollar in an arm-wrestling match."
One of the 10-year-old boys was admitted to the hospital for more than 5 days for treatment of severe internal injuries, Feldman said.
He alleged that his investigation showed the camp was largely unsupervised and day-to-day operations were left to inexperienced teenagers, who received little or no training as camp counsellors.
Scouts spokesman Gary Laermer said the organisation was "very careful selecting counsellors, including interviews, screenings and reference checking" for day and seasonal staff.

Feldman said two 13-year-old boys had been arrested for the assault and would face criminal action in family court in Sullivan County, New York. Details of any proceedings have not been made public because the defendants are minors.

The complaint asks for $72 million for the mothers of four of the six boys, charging the Boy Scouts with negligence, loss of service, negligent infliction of emotional distress, intentional infliction of emotional distress and punitive damages to be decided by a jury.
Feldman told reporters that the alleged negligence was compounded by the alleged failure of any Boy Scouts of America official to tell the parents about the incidents.
But the Scouts spokesman said that "immediately when we were made aware of the alleged incidents we told the authorities in Narrowsburg and every effort was made to reach the parents."
He said the organisation was able to reach only one of the three parents immediately and the others were reached once the boys had returned to their homes in the Bronx and Manhattan.
The parents said they found out about the attacks from other children or the boys themselves when they returned home after the week-long camp.

"My son can't sleep, he's afraid to go places without me. It's not right for any child," said Denise Palmer, mother of one of the boys allegedly assaulted. "I was told by other children about the incident. The police and the hospital did not call."
The defendants named in the complaint are the Boy Scouts of America, the National Council of the Boy Scouts of America and New York State and city affiliates of the Boy Scouts.
